slices.rationale: Project open owns serde migration through the tracked domain types; the planned matrix is required because current tests do not cover every documented field plus save/reopen.
The router already owns Host, Origin and body guards, but the listener accepts a caller supplied address and no protocol-version middleware is present.
Tracked validators cover several shapes and byte import, but URL import is explicitly unsupported rather than HTTPS-only streamed with typed MIME and a 1 GiB decoded cap.
Bridge errors flow into the LLM-facing result conversion and currently retain raw path and IO detail.
Open currently unwraps an absent generation log to default without seeding manifest generation provenance.
This record is an exact six-test evidence requirement; the Unix target still includes the unsupported backend and only component-name tests are tracked.
The Windows target is still an unsupported include; the three records form the ordered scaffold, backend, and STATUS_PENDING invariant slice.
This is a process/evidence contract with exact receipt confinement and live API validation, not a product feature.
These headings repeat the broader project-open assembly acceptance; the remaining concrete gaps are represented by legacy-default and generation-seed slices.
These records span MCP, safe filesystem, playback, export and Agent clients; they must be acceptance collections over child slices rather than one implementation owner.
The assembly document says corrupt media.json is nonfatal, while upstream analysis and tracked code require malformed manifest to fail; acceptance must be corrected before product work.
The stable lowercase 32-hex identity and missing-file behavior are implemented and directly tested.
All ten headings describe the same tracked EditorState to EditCommand to AppCore to EventBus ownership path with undo and version tests.
The domain resolver owns expected-path resolution and the Tauri projection distinguishes present and missing state.
The tracked conversion helpers use Math.round and violate the truncation contract at fractional boundaries.
The shared settings command exists, but the import-time decision and mismatch UI contract are not connected.
Detection exists, but auto-cut always returns a read-only preview and has no atomic write path.
These three records duplicate one transport implementation slice and should share the data-safety MCP transport owner.
The records are duplicate command-contract views of the same validation and safe URL import slice.
This is the command-contract duplicate of the data-safety redaction slice.
The version-ordered event to refresh path exists, but a whole-store architectural proof is still missing.
Focused gesture tests exist, but no closed inventory proves every component emits the exact shared DTO.
Many DTO cases are individually tested, but no exhaustive Rust mapping and frontend invoke-handler parity gate exists.
These headings span beat sync, smart reframe, tighten and shared failure semantics; they must aggregate child capability records and cannot be closed by the beat slice alone.
Each record mixes Rust project authority with UI-only persistence; authority belongs to the mirror slice and persistence belongs to home-shell.
These nine records are shell layout and titlebar behavior and should be owned by home-shell rather than command contracts.
These unchecked historical implementation steps were superseded by the current audit CLI and should be marked obsolete rather than scheduled as product work.
Tagged core events are forwarded and WebView emit errors are intentionally ignored as nonfatal.
Home currently filters missing entries during load and the card only removes a recent entry; persistent missing, reveal and safe-trash states need a shared registry.
New and open helpers exist, while sample materialization, rollback, recent registration and tutorial routing remain one vertical flow.
All three layout components exist, but no tracked test proves pinned geometry, gutters, radii and focus treatment.
Persistence helpers exist, while the current uiStore tests cover playback rather than restart-safe layout, panel and keyframe state.
The menu owner is tracked but its complete command, shortcut, state and disabled-rule contract lacks focused evidence.
This record combines registry, cards, samples, welcome and update surfaces and must be decomposed into child acceptance records.
Autosave and close-flush have implementation evidence, while Home project metadata remains a registry gap; the record must split before completion.
Every-component mapping is an acceptance index across the shell, not a single implementation owner.
The current DTO and card primarily expose missing state; the complete generation, download, failure and border-precedence state machine is absent.
Backend skipped and recursive-folder contracts exist, but visible unsupported and folder-failure feedback is not proved.
Core thumbnail and sprite paths exist, while invalid geometry and the full service/cache/concurrency acceptance path remain unproved.

Disk format and UI bars are tested, but no deterministic PCM fixture jointly proves sample count, RMS normalization, orientation and cache, including format/source discrimination between valid all-silent cache data and poisoned legacy output; all == 1.0 alone cannot classify the cache.
Library primitives exist, but several rail destinations remain disabled or placeholders and no complete workflow acceptance test exists.
This record spans import, preview, drag, favorite, rename, delete and persistence and must aggregate child slices.
This record combines FFmpeg, thumbnail and waveform acceptance and is not one implementation owner.
Manifest v2 persistence and legacy missing version and array defaults are implemented and directly tested.
This is the media-library duplicate of the completed data-safety cache identity requirement.
Supported files remain importable with default metadata when probing fails.
Relink preserves the asset id, validates type before mutation and clears missing state.
A nested clip reference and recursive render-plan flattening do not exist; the same plan must feed preview and export.
The report identified no current optical-flow backend; source-frame interpolation must enter the shared resolver path.
Linear and circular mask paths exist, while polygon masks are deliberately encoded as a no-op and need shared preview/export proof.
No tracked stabilization analyzer or command owner exists; the solution must be represented as editable crop or transform state.
Effect metadata reaches the render plan but the generic effect chain has no production pass implementation.
Both records describe one missing editable transition model and overlap render pass.
Representation and shader code exist, but the record should remain incomplete until GPU output is checked against the CPU reference.
No tracked HSL-secondary representation or render path was found.
No validated LUT import, persisted reference, GPU 3D texture or preview/export path exists.
PCM, playback and export owners exist, but no loudness analysis or normalization target path exists.
No tracked denoise node exists; playback and export must consume the same processing owner.
No stem separation implementation was found; results must re-enter the shared media import and provenance path.
Current chunking serves cancellation loops but the whole timeline mix is still allocated in memory.
The tracked renderer is a fail-closed skeleton and explicitly reports that live Chromium is not implemented.
Substantial text rendering and structural tests exist, while the module document still lists fallback and layout parity work.
The media crate explicitly defers the runtime queue; current Tauri search code does not prove a bounded serialized production coordinator.
Runtime path helpers exist, but no verified packaged external-binary configuration or macOS and Windows execution receipt was found.
Image materialization exists, while all three production resolver paths return None for Lottie.
MediaEngine exposes several services, while decode and encode remain mostly flat exports and dependency direction lacks a closed contract test.
This record combines 50-track performance, curve speed, nested sequences, multicam alignment and optical flow; nested and optical have child records and the other three need new child records.
HDR, proxy media and account state belong to three different product owners and must be split.
Renderer, packaging, settings, solo and stub debt cannot be owned or accepted as one implementation slice.
Packaged macOS and Windows release readiness is a cross-slice runtime evidence gate, not one product implementation.
Transitions, masks, LUT and curves have independent owners and child slices.
This record mixes polygon masks and generic effects, which are already represented by separate mask and effect slices.
These are architecture principle and compliance headings; they should become verifier or acceptance collections rather than feature records.
Both add and insert command paths directly prove that a probed silent video does not create linked audio.
Capability routing, WebKit and Rust ownership, session identity, retained-frame handoff and source identity have direct focused tests.
Both id shapes and absent optional fields are handled and directly tested.
The media crate deliberately uses ffmpeg-sidecar and does not link a libav ABI binding.
Frame decoding is injected through a closure and the production crate does not own an image decoder dependency.
Missing or corrupt decoder output is represented as an absent source frame.
Both stub and unavailable Chromium paths enforce document size before rendering or returning unavailable.
The dependency-free PNG encoder is deterministic and tested for dimensions and alpha.
The narrower optional-field and explicit-version migration contract has direct project and domain tests, though broader exhaustive migration remains in data-safety.
Typed state events cross the Tauri bridge and raw frame pixels remain on the separate playback transport.
Probe, frame decode, PCM extraction and encoding have tracked end-to-end FFmpeg integration fixtures.

tests.name: offers all four interchange formats with their extensions and commands

slices.rationale: FCPXML and XMEML, OTIO and EDL all have tracked exporters, Tauri and frontend routing, and format tests.
